metadata.creator: Upham, Alfred H.
metadata.description: Alfred H. Upham, president of Miami University, writes to Murray Sheehan of the Royal Thai Legation about Sheehan's planned attendance at Commencement. Upham states that a reservation is being made for Sheehan in David Swing Hall and regrets that there will not be at least one boy from Thailand in the graduating class or that the Minister could be secured as speaker.
metadata.title: Letter to Mr. Murray Sheehan from the president, 26 May 1942
metadata.transcript:
[page 1]
May 26, 1942

Mr. [Mister] Murray Sheehan
Royal Thai Legation
2300 Kalorama Road
Washington, D. C. [District of Columbia]

Dear Murray:

I am delighted to know that you are coming on for Commencement. We shall all be glad to see you and I think you will find yourself very comfortable in David Swing Hall where we are making a reservation for you.

It is too bad that we cannot have at least one boy from Thailand in the graduating class while you are here, particularly since we were unable to secure the Minister as our speaker.

Cordially yours,

President
